Take this free CAT Simple and Compound Interest online test — 10 exam-pattern MCQs with instant scoring and a worked explanation for every answer. The Simple & Compound Interest chapter is a high-yield part of the CAT Quantitative Aptitude section, and a favourite in XAT, SNAP, NMAT and CMAT too. This guide explains what CAT Simple & Compound Interest tests, the formulas and shortcuts worth memorising, the mistakes that cost marks, and a free 10-question online test you can take right now.

Take the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter e-book at the end for full, exam-level practice.

What CAT asks on Simple & Compound Interest

Simple interest, compound interest (annual and more frequent), the CI–SI difference, and growth / depreciation.

Key formulas & shortcuts

  • SI = P·R·T/100; CI: A = P(1 + R/100)ᵀ.
  • For 2 years, CI − SI = P(R/100)².
  • Rule of 72: money doubles in about 72/R years.
  • For the same P, R, T, CI ≥ SI (equal only in year 1).

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Using the SI formula where compounding is intended.
  • Forgetting to adjust R and T when compounding is half-yearly/quarterly.
  • Mixing up amount and interest.

faq.q: What is the quick CI−SI difference for 2 years?
faq.a: P(R/100)². For 3 years it is P(R/100)²(3 + R/100).

faq.q: How does half-yearly compounding change the formula?
faq.a: Use rate R/2 and time 2T (i.e. A = P(1 + R/200)^{2T}).
